Consult Summary:
- Video consult for recent bee/wasp sting to arm with localized rash and anxiety; no clinical signs of anaphylaxis observed; advised OTC antihistamines and red-flag precautions.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sting to arm a few minutes prior to call with localized redness/rash; concerned about breathing and possible lip swelling.
- Associated symptoms: Blotchy rash and puncture mark at sting site; right-sided lip soreness/tingling; tongue feels “weird”; initial anxiety with perceived breathing difficulty but not acute at time of consult.
- Pertinent negatives: No significant local swelling; no current dyspnea observed; no prior anaphylaxis; no EpiPen; no known food or pet allergies; family history noncontributory for acute reactions. No medications taken for this episode.
- Past medical history: Eczema. Intermittent anxiety/panic episodes (no medications).
- Allergies: Penicillin.
- Social history: Works as a computer scientist; lives alone; has a cat.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- General/respiratory: Breathing appeared normal on video; speaking comfortably.
- Oropharynx/lips: No visible lip or airway soft tissue swelling on video exam; throat exam unremarkable.
- Skin (sting site, arm): Mild erythema with puncture mark; blotchy rash; no significant swelling observed.

Impression:
- Localized allergic reaction to bee/wasp sting; anxiety symptoms. No evidence of anaphylaxis at time of assessment.

Plan:
- Medications: Start OTC antihistamine—chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet, up to six times daily; route not documented. Alternatively, a once-daily antihistamine (name/dose not documented).
- Safety-netting: Seek urgent care/ED immediately if lip/tongue swelling progresses, breathing difficulty, or stridor occurs. If symptoms worsen rapidly, go directly to ED; otherwise arrange follow-up as needed.
- Local care/monitoring: If arm redness spreads, becomes hot, or other signs of local infection develop, seek reassessment; antibiotics may be needed (none prescribed today).
- Testing: No immediate need for allergy testing; consider if reactions recur.
- Education: Provided information link on anaphylaxis warning signs.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: Vitals not recorded; comprehensive medication list/reconciliation not completed; past surgical history not obtained; smoking/alcohol history not obtained; immunization status not reviewed; route for antihistamine not specified.
- Internal conflicts: Patient stated age 27 and DOB 11/17/1991—conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Minor hesitations; overall clear and interpretable.
